cue: The contrasts suggest an exception allowing an uncertified reseller to buy refrigerant. I anticipate a resale-only restriction and purchaser identity/address record; the omitted stem could change this.

With no quantity or operation specified, these numbers cannot identify an answer. I choose 20 mL from a weak expectation of a round equipment fluid tolerance; I do not recall a reliable matching standard. This is an uncertain domain expectation, not a detected wording cue.

I anticipate a moisture-contaminated system or exhausted moisture absorber scenario, for which replacing desiccant is the targeted action. Each other action could be appropriate for another omitted scenario.

These roles suggest responsibility for used refrigerant transferred from a salvage vehicle. I anticipate that the shop charging the receiving vehicle must ensure proper processing, rather than relying on the extraction facility.

The ownership contrasts suggest a shared-equipment exception among related garage locations. Common owner-operator ownership seems the likely condition, though I cannot establish the exception from options alone.

I anticipate a question about evaporator cooling, which absorbs heat as liquid refrigerant vaporizes. All four describe physically possible heat transfers, so choosing the evaporator process relies on anticipating the stem.
The explicit initial 15% charge distractor suggests the omitted scenario is a successful preliminary leak check during R-1234yf charging. I anticipate proceeding with the remainder of the charge.

I anticipate a flushing-agent approval or compatibility-standard question. Material compatibility seems the narrow claim such a specification would establish, whereas debris removal and OEM suitability depend on additional conditions.

I anticipate a regulatory distinction involving opening MVAC-like off-road cab systems for repairs. The options form a balanced two-by-two comparison and give no surface answer cue; my choice depends on that imagined regulatory scenario.

R-1234yf is mildly flammable, so ignition within a concentration range is a distinctive known fact in this category. The other statements are also plausible refrigerant properties; this selection assumes the omitted question concerns its special safety hazard.

I anticipate an equipment certification or compliance-verification question that requires observing the technician actually operating the machine. Attestation and job records would not directly demonstrate that operation, but a different stem could favor them.

I anticipate a replacement-component oil quantity or specification that differs from factory guidance. Instructions supplied with the replacement would then be the most directly applicable authority; without that scenario the workshop manual would also be plausible.

The alternatives suggest a recovery-filter replacement interval. Refrigerant mass processed is a plausible filter loading measure; elapsed hours or pressure-test dates address other maintenance concerns.

I anticipate the prerequisite immediately before opening or replacing a refrigerant filter. Clearing refrigerant from the existing filter is the relevant preparation, while reaching capacity indicates the need for replacement rather than readiness to open it.
